newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-EMBARRASSED SOUTH AFRICA FORCED TO DROP FISH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EMBARRASSED SOUTH AFRICA FORCED TO DROP FISH.

text.p: Embarrassed South African soccer officials have had to drop Italian-based defender Mark Fish from their squad for Saturday's World Cup qualifying match in Zambia after belatedly discovering he is suspended for the game

Fish, 23, flew in from Rome to Johannesburg on Tuesday only to be told by officials he would not be playing in the group three match in Lusaka on Saturday after picking up two yellow cards in South Africa's three previous qualifying matches.
World Cup rules stipulate an automatic one-match suspension for players who receive two cautions in qualifying ties but South African officials were unaware of the rules until Monday.
Fish, who plays for Italian Serie A club Lazio, was booked against Malawi in June and again in November when South Africa beat Zaire 1-0 in their group three qualifier in Johannesburg.

A fax from FIFA informing the South African Football Association (SAFA) of the suspension lay unattended in the association's office until Monday when they reopened after the Christmas holidays. It was too late then to stop Fish from boarding his flight in Rome.
Uncapped defender Bradley Muir has been called up to replace Fish in the 19-man squad which leaves for Lusaka on Thursday.
